detail:
Why Is Cloudflare Stock Rallying Today?
Fiona Craig
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 5:28 AM PST 2 min read
NET
Trade NET on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
AI circuit ©Adobe Stock Images

Shares of Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) rose 4.4% to $295.79 in pre-market trading on Friday, supported by a broader recovery across technology stocks and a recent positive assessment from investment firm TD Cowen.

The advance follows several weeks of selling pressure that pushed shares in the cloud infrastructure and cybersecurity company significantly below their 52-week high of $370.35.

Why Has TD Cowen Named Cloudflare Its Top Infrastructure Software Pick?

Earlier this week, TD Cowen designated Cloudflare as its preferred infrastructure software stock for 2027, maintaining a Buy rating and a $375 price target.

The investment firm highlighted the strength of Cloudflare's global technology platform, increasing adoption among enterprise customers and expanding opportunities associated with artificial intelligence workloads.

In particular, TD Cowen identified the company's Workers AI offering as an important component of its longer-term growth prospects.

The broader analyst consensus also remains positive, with the average price target above Cloudflare's current trading level.

How Is the Broader Technology Recovery Supporting Cloudflare?

Cloudflare's advance coincided with a recovery across US equities, with the S&P 500 gaining 1.8% and the Nasdaq advancing 2.4%.

Renewed buying interest in growth-oriented technology companies following recent market losses has provided additional support for Cloudflare.

The stock has an estimated beta of between 1.8 and 2.0, indicating that its share price has historically exhibited greater volatility than the broader market.

Is Short Interest Contributing to Cloudflare's Recovery?

Cloudflare has experienced a recent increase in short interest, creating the potential for short covering during periods of rising share prices.

Short covering occurs when investors who have previously sold borrowed shares repurchase them to close their positions, potentially contributing to additional buying pressure.

However, the extent to which short covering contributed to Friday's pre-market advance remains unclear.

What Should Investors Watch Next?

Despite the latest recovery, Cloudflare shares remain significantly below their 52-week high of $370.35.

Investors continue to monitor enterprise adoption of the company's technology platform, demand for its artificial intelligence services and the sustainability of the broader technology sector recovery.

While TD Cowen's positive assessment and improving market sentiment have supported the latest advance, Cloudflare's share price remains sensitive to changes in investor risk appetite and technology sector valuations.

Key Takeaways

Argus cut its CrowdStrike price target to $350 from $425 on Nov. 24 and kept its Buy rating, a target 67% above the last close.

A day earlier, CrowdStrike reported record net new ARR of $419 million and agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion.

The deal takes CrowdStrike into network security against Cloudflare and adds roughly 19% more CrowdStrike shares, with a close not expected until January 2028.

On estimates for the year ending January 2029, $350 is 161x earnings, well above CrowdStrike's five-year average of 109x, so the Street's $249 average is the better guide for the next year.

CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) just reported the best quarter in its history, yet the stock sits 27% below its October high. On Nov. 24, Argus cut its target to $350 from $425 and kept its Buy rating, still 67% above the last close of $209.30.

The day before, CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler (ZS:NASDAQ) for about $43.9 billion in stock, taking it into network security against rivals like Cloudflare (NET:NYSE).

Record numbers, with a big deal attached

On Nov. 23, CrowdStrike posted record net new ARR of $419 million for the quarter ended Oct. 31, up 58%, and raised its full-year growth outlook for net new ARR to 45% at the midpoint. Free cash flow hit a record $474 million.

Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each of theirs, roughly 19% more CrowdStrike shares, and the deal isn't expected to close until January 2028.

The deal also puts the combined company up against Cloudflare, whose third-quarter revenue grew 39%. Can one laptop-to-network platform win over Cloudflare's zero-trust customers?

Argus stands well above the pack

Even after the cut, $350 sits well above the other targets set on Nov. 24. Wells Fargo cut its target to $265 from $300. BTIG cut to $239 from $312, and StoneX to $250 from $325.
